newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hanwa Bank traded for first time after suspension.
newsitem.headline: Hanwa Bank traded for first time after suspension.

text.p: Hanwa Bank Ltd shares were traded on Thursday afternoon for the first time since the Finance Ministry suspended most of its business last week.
At 0515 GMT, the shares stood at five yen on the Osaka bourse, after being ask-only at 26 yen on Wednesday.

Last Thursday, the Ministry of Finance announced that it had halted operations at the second-tier regional bank based in western Japan, except for withdrawals of deposits, because the bank could not recover its bad loans and was unable to operate as a going concern.
The Osaka Securities Exchange later announced that the bank's shares would be delisted on February 22.
